title: Proportional fair pacing with stochastic probe escrow to reduce queue starvation
author: Priya Rao
release_notes: Introduce proportional per-queue pacing and stochastic probe escrow to mitigate starvation and reduce p99 tail latency under mixed KV-heavy workloads. No API changes.
description: Motivation: Continuous batching scheduler occasionally starves small, latency-sensitive queues when KV-heavy or long-seq requests dominate. Prior fixes focused on static slot reservations and deadline nudging; those reduce starvation but either waste capacity or increase p50. This PR implements a proportional-share pacing allocator plus a stochastic probe escrow that injects small, jittered probe windows to detect under-served queues and re-balance without large reserved slots. Design: 1) Each queue is assigned a lightweight weight computed from a configurable priority + recent serviced tokens (EWMA). The allocator computes proportional token budgets per scheduling epoch which guide admission and slice sizes. 2) A probe escrow is maintained as a small fractional budget (configurable, default 3% of epoch tokens) split into jittered micro-windows that are opportunistically offered to candidate queues that have had low recent service. Probes are intentionally stochastic to avoid synchronized bursts across workers. 3) When a probe window uncovers backlog, the allocator temporarily bumps the queue weight for the next N epochs to allow draining; if the queue is empty, escrow is re-credited. 4) Integration with KV cache: probes are lightweight and attempt to warm the KV pin for the queue without triggering full model inflations; the KV-prefetch hint path was extended to be probe-aware and marked in traces. 5) Observability: new metrics: scheduler.queue_ewma_tokens, scheduler.probe_escrow_utilization, scheduler.probe_hits, scheduler.probe_misses. Implementation notes: - Runtime changes are limited to scheduler/core and scheduler/allocator modules. - Added a micro state machine for probes to avoid re-entrancy and races across worker threads. - Kept the continuous-batcher admission contract identical (no public API changes). Tests and performance: - Microbench: synthetic mix of 80% large KV-pin requests (seq len 2048, heavy KV accesses) + 20% small latency-sensitive requests (seq len 32). - Canary run in perf-canary harness across 8 GPUs, 10k rps sustained for 30 minutes. Results: p50 latency ~unchanged (-2ms), p95 improved by ~6ms, p99 improved by ~28ms in mixed load compared to baseline with static soft reservations; throughput unchanged within 1%. Starvation incidents detected by SLO checker dropped from 16 to 1 per hour in this workload. KV cache hit-rate remained within noise (+0.3%). Backwards compatibility and operational controls: - Feature gated behind runtime flag scheduler.proportional_pacing.enabled=false by default in older clusters; enabled in canary. - Two tuning knobs exposed: scheduler.proportional_pacing.escrow_fraction and scheduler.proportional_pacing.jitter_window_ms. - Default knobs selected after grid search described in the PR. Please add a clear invariant comment about escrow re-crediting to avoid surprises during preemption.; Priya Rao: Added invariant comments and a unit test covering preemption and re-credit in probe_escrow_test.go.; Diego Martinez: Found a race when two workers try to claim the same probe window; could cause double-service of lightweight probes and corrupt EWMA counters.; Priya Rao: Fixed by introducing a CAS-backed probe lease and added test; also added an integration canary that reproduces the scenario.; Sofia Nguyen: Can we expose probe metrics at token granularity and add a dashboard tile?; Priya Rao: Metrics added and a Grafana tile in observability/dashboards/scheduler-probes.json; added alert scheduler.probe_escrow_utilization_high (warn) to ops runbook.; Jordan Kim: CI flaky on perf-canary step (timing-dependent) — reran and it passed.; Diego Martinez: Approved after fixes.; Jordan Kim: Approved and requested squash merge.; Release manager: Merged via squash and bumped runtime minor version.

notes_on_rollback: Feature is behind flag; rollback is simply disabling scheduler.proportional_pacing.enabled or scaling down to previous runtime; no DB migrations required.
risk_assessment: Medium: allocator math changes touch core scheduling path; mitigated by conservative defaults, canary rollout, and feature flag. Race scenarios discovered and fixed during review.
post_merge_actions: Enable flag in 10% of clusters for 24h, monitor scheduler.probe_escrow_utilization, scheduler.queue_ewma_tokens, and SLO alerts; if anomalies, disable flag and revert config; follow-up task ENG-3340 to sweep knobs across regions.
